title: Taking your AI to the edge with .NET MAUI | OD803

segments.text: GERALD VERSLUIS: Hello and welcome to this session
about taking your AI to the edge with.NET MAUI.
My name is Gerald and I work here at Microsoft
on the.NET team, specifically on the.NET MAUI team.
And in this session, we're going to see what the current state
of MAUI is in.NET 10, what we've been building,
what to expect from.NET 11, but also how we as a team became
so much more productive with the use of Copilot,
how you can be more productive building your.NET MAUI apps
with the tools that we're putting out there,
and how you can deliver that value to your end customer.
So let's dig in.
For a quick reminder, quick refresher for the people
who might be new seeing this,
what is this.NET MAUI thing again?
.NET MAUI stands for.NET Multiplatform App UI,
and that is our offering
to build cross-platform amazing looking apps on iOS, Android,
Windows, and macOS through C Sharp and.NET.
So we have single project, single code base.
So you just have a single project to launch all of these,
to reach all of these projects, all of these platforms,
which is really, really amazing.
It all maps to native controls and native styling
on the platform exactly as you would expect on the platform
that you're running on.
It feels and looks exactly as it's supposed to be
on the operating system, on the device that you're running on.
We have, like, all kinds of devices, APIs you can reach
with that unified C Sharp and.NET layer.
You can get the geolocation, you can get the flashlights,
you can get the file system, all these kinds of things,
all built in, and lots and lots of controls already.
So everything you need to build cross-platform apps
that are useful for everyone.
Then we also have something that is called Blazor Hybrid.
And with that, you can take your existing Blazor offering,
your existing Blazor application,
put that in a Blazor Hybrid WebView, and then package
that as a mobile app and put that in the stores,
have that little icon on the screen, without having to lose
or reinvent anything, because you can just take your existing
Blazor app, or if you just have this one very specific Blazor
control that you have, that you've created, and you want
to reuse that in your.NET MAUI app,
you can absolutely do that as well.
The choice is yours.
We have options for everyone.
You can make your full app a hybrid application with Blazor.
You can just have this little part
of your application be a little Blazor Hybrid application,
and the rest is fully native,
and it will integrate seamlessly.
You will not be able to tell the difference.
And if you want to take it even a step further,
and you maybe have like a React Native, an Angular,
or some other JavaScript application,
we have something for that as well.
We have the hybrid WebView there too.
So lots and lots of options for everyone,
depending on where you are in your development lifecycle,
what you want to do there.

for every audience, right?
If you want to go for reach, then you probably want to go
with Blazor, like Blazor in the web browser.
Everything that runs a web browser,
you can take your Blazor app there.

very powerful combination.
